title: The grind of the small band and who is still alive
summary: Moore notes the smaller band's work was a grind and discusses surviving members.

story.theme_name: Working with and around Louis Armstrong
story.community_name: Playing with and around Louis Armstrong

blocks.x: Every theatre we went in the brought 'em in world there for Louie/there was standing room only. And we got so tired from working, but it's a happy tiredness because we knew along with Louie we knew that we were liked everywhere we went and at one time Joe Darensbourg left and Eddie Shu took his place. That was the only people that left. Let's see, now, Arvell Shaw left for a while, too and Jack Lesberg took his place.
But I guess it was really a grind that time. I mean it was much more of a grind than the first time you were with Louie back in the '40s.
And it was a smaller group, there were only six pieces.

Yes. Yes. Now that I'm semi-retired I think of my days that I met Armstrong, all the rest -- I mean not always Armstrong, all the rest of the people that I have associated with in my musical life. Some are still alive, some are gone. You can name the people -- you know the people that have left us. Out of that Armstrong band is, I think,
S. & S. REPORTING COMPANY, INC. WOrth 2-2915 WOrth 2-2943
I think Joe Darenbourg is still alive.
I think Joe is living in Los Angeles.
In California, that's right. And the banjo player and guitar player was Glenn Thompson.
And Arvell is still active. Let's say, okay -- Fiji -- did you play Fiji?
No, we didn't play Fiji at all. We didn't play Honolulu either. We just jumped from San Francisco to New Zealand.
